---
title: "aws-emulator vs real AWS"
subtitle: "Every behaviour difference found, and whether it is specific to the emulator"
---

{{< include _generated/version-box.md >}}

::: {.big-warning}
**The most important difference: Lambda functions do not run the way they do on AWS.**
aws-emulator executes Python handlers on **RustPython**, an embedded interpreter inside the
emulator process (`sys.implementation.name == "rustpython"`, reporting Python 3.14-alpha even for
`python3.12`), and Node.js handlers on QuickJS. Consequences:

- no native extensions: numpy, GDAL/rasterio, pydantic-core, cryptography and asyncpg can't load;
- no sockets and no `asyncio`;
- no layers for Python, and no container-image functions;
- no Java, Ruby or custom (`provided.al2023`) runtimes.

**Real titiler and real tipg cannot run on aws-emulator.** This experiment uses pure-Python
stand-ins with the same API surface. Anything you validate on the emulator only says something
about pure-Python or JS handler code.
:::

How to read this page:

- **Scope.** *emulator only* means real AWS behaves differently: it is a fidelity gap.
  **also on AWS** means a design constraint you'd hit in production too.
- **Status.** *works* means it behaved like AWS, *partial* means usable with a workaround, *gap*
  means it doesn't work.
- **Source and evidence.** Rows come from [`findings.toml`](https://github.com/ashiklom/simon-code-research/blob/main/aws-emulator-tofu/findings.toml).
  Evidence links point to the [capability probes](probes.qmd), the [end-to-end matrix](auth-api.qmd#results-on-aws-emulator)
  or the [deploy cycle](emulator.qmd#deploy-cycle).

The questions raised in planning, answered:

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| HTTP API v2 JWT authorizer not checking signatures: emulator or general? | **Emulator only.** On AWS the JWT authorizer verifies the signature against the issuer's JWKS. On the emulator, a payload-edited token and a token signed by an unrelated key both got 200. |
| CloudFront not forwarding `Authorization`: all CloudFront, or the emulator? | **Mostly the emulator.** On AWS, `Authorization` *is* forwarded when it's in the **cache policy** (cache key). An origin request policy alone can't forward it, and that part is real AWS behaviour. The emulator drops it whatever the policy says. |
| CloudFront dropping origin response headers? | **Emulator only.** AWS passes origin headers (Content-Type, Cache-Control, CORS) through. |
| Aurora without PostGIS? | **Emulator only.** Aurora PostgreSQL supports PostGIS; the emulator's engine is SQLite behind a PostgreSQL wire protocol. |
| Lambda can't run titiler/tipg? | **Emulator only.** On AWS both run as container images or zip/layer packages. |
